The annual law that funds the State Department and foreign assistance, including the security assistance accounts that pay for [Foreign Military Financing](fmf.qmd), [IMET](imet.qmd), and [Peacekeeping Operations](pko-551.qmd). Its general provisions, numbered from Sec. 7001, carry many of the standing conditions on foreign aid, such as the [coup restriction](sec7008-coup.qmd). Foreign assistance has had its own annual appropriation since the first one under the [Foreign Assistance Act](faa-1961.qmd), the Foreign Assistance and Related Agencies Appropriation Act, 1962 (Pub. L. 87-329).

:::

## Key provisions

- Title I: Department of State and related programs. Title II: administration of assistance. Title III: bilateral economic assistance.
- Title IV: international security assistance, including International Military Education and Training, the Foreign Military Financing Program, and Peacekeeping Operations.
- Titles V and VI: multilateral assistance, and export and investment assistance.
- Title VII general provisions: notification of the Appropriations Committees 15 days before obligating funds beyond justified amounts, the coup restriction in Sec. 7008, and country-specific conditions.

## Why it matters

Much foreign policy is made here rather than in authorizing law. Congress has not enacted a comprehensive foreign assistance authorization in decades, so the annual act, through its accounts, earmarks, notification rules, and conditions, is the main way it shapes aid. The [Leahy Laws](leahy-laws.qmd) began as a rider to this act. For staff, the act's general provisions and the joint explanatory statement are usually the controlling text for how a program may be run in a given year.

## Current status

The most recent full-year act is for fiscal year 2026, enacted as Division F of Pub. L. 119-75 under the House's name for the bill, the National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026. Fiscal year 2027 began under the continuing resolution in Pub. L. 119-103. Check current status.

[Last checked November 24, 2026.]{.checked}

## Where it sits

- **Layer.** Specific authorization. Laws aimed at a particular conflict, country, program, or problem. Most work through a framework statute: an AUMF through the War Powers Resolution, a sanctions act through IEEPA. ([How the layers work](../study/index.qmd#the-authority-stack))
- **Builds on.** [Constitution (war powers)](constitution-war-powers.qmd), [Foreign Assistance Act](faa-1961.qmd), [Arms Export Control Act](aeca-1976.qmd).
- **Built upon by.** [Coup restriction (Sec. 7008)](sec7008-coup.qmd), [Foreign Military Financing](fmf.qmd), [IMET](imet.qmd), [Peacekeeping Operations](pko-551.qmd).
- **Codified in.** [Title 22 U.S.C.](title22-usc.qmd).
- **Era.** Building the national security state ([timeline](../study/timeline.qmd)).
- **Study.** [Unit 4: The power of the purse](../study/units/purse.qmd) (core reading).
- **Who's involved.** [House Appropriations](../whos-who.qmd#hac), [Senate Appropriations](../whos-who.qmd#sac).
